text_blocks.snippet: Hemorrhagic stroke occurs when a blood vessel in the brain ruptures, causing bleeding into the brain tissue. There are three main types of hemorrhagic stroke:

list.snippet: Occurs when a blood vessel within the brain substance ruptures.
Most common type of hemorrhagic stroke.
Symptoms may include severe headache, sudden weakness or numbness on one side of the body, confusion, and loss of consciousness.
Occurs when a blood vessel on the surface of the brain ruptures, causing bleeding into the space between the brain and the skull (subarachnoid space).
Often caused by an aneurysm (a weakened spot in the blood vessel wall).
Symptoms may include sudden, severe headache, nausea, vomiting, stiff neck, and sensitivity to light.
Occurs when a blood vessel bleeds into the ventricles (fluid-filled spaces) in the brain.
Less common than ICH and SAH.
Symptoms may vary depending on the location and size of the bleed, but may include headache, confusion, seizures, and coma.

text_blocks.snippet: It's important to note that other types of hemorrhagic stroke may exist, such as perimesencephalic hemorrhage and brainstem hemorrhage. The specific type of hemorrhagic stroke depends on the location of the bleed in the brain.
